title: Decimal to Per Cent
description: Read a decimal as hundredths on hundred grids, and write the number of hundredths as the per cent with the % sign kept.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Write a decimal as a per cent by reading it as hundredths, with the % sign kept, including tenths, decimals above one and whole numbers.
writeup.look: A decimal card over a row of hundred grids, one for each whole, the Hundredths counter, a fraction card and a per cent card, and the % sign tile.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Decimal to Per Cent' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the Hundredths counter, the hundredths shaded across every grid. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The decimal card stands at x 110, y 220, 300 by 110, its digits deep blue and its point in near-black ink, with a grey 0 labelled Place holder wherever a zero holds a place open. Up to four hundred grids, each 220 by 220, stand in a row from x 110, y 400, 30 apart, each labelled Whole and 100%. Cells fill deep blue, whole grids first. The Hundredths counter stands at x 450, y 230, with the % sign tile in its tray at x 450, y 310. The Read as hundredths and Split tenths buttons stand at x 690, y 230 and x 690, y 310. When a tenth is split, its column is cut into ten cells counted in amber. The fraction card and the per cent card stand at x 930, y 220 and x 930, y 310, and the per cent card turns green when it matches. Until the sign tile is placed, the per cent card shows that many whole grids, faded to half strength. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key and a % key, for typing a decimal, a whole number or a per cent. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. The part the question gives, as shaded cells, a fraction, a decimal or an amount, is deep blue, labelled Given. The per cent, fraction or decimal the working reaches, and what is left after a part is used, is green, labelled Answer or Left. Both terms multiplied or divided by one number, and the times one hundred step before the % sign, are vermilion, labelled Both terms or Times 100. A unit fact that puts two amounts in one unit is violet, labelled Unit fact. The part used, taken away or not won is rose, labelled Used or Not won. The step, cell or number being worked on now is amber. A zero holding a place open inside a decimal is grey, labelled Place holder, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded cell of a whole stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the % sign is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The cards show the last decimal beside its hundredths and its per cent, with the grids filled under it.

phases.win: the counter stops at sixty-two, and the cards read 62/100 and 62%
phases.does: taps Read as hundredths, reads the counter, types the per cent and places the % sign
phases.goal: a decimal with two places is a number of hundredths, and that number is the per cent
phases.says: Read it as hundredths. How many hundredths is it?
phases.check: Away from the screen: how would you read nought point three nine as hundredths?
phases.feels: the counter and the per cent card landing on the same number
phases.hands: Read a decimal aloud as hundredths, shade that many cells of a paper grid, and write the count with the % sign.
phases.tries: First rung: read the tenths digit and count that many full columns. Second rung: read the hundredths digit and count that many more cells. Third rung: the same task with fewer hundredths, before the full decimal returns.

wrong.why: the decimal is the number given, so the sign seems to belong on it
wrong.move: puts the % sign straight onto the decimal
wrong.screen: a second grid beside the first shades what the child's answer names, less than a single cell, and the counter's own count is lit amber

wrong.why: the count looks like the answer
wrong.move: types the count of hundredths without the % sign
wrong.screen: the per cent card shows that many whole grids faded to half strength, and the sign tile pulses once in its tray

phases.screen: the card showing 0.62 over one empty grid, and the % sign tile beside the per cent card
phases.soWhat: a decimal with two places is a number of hundredths, and that number is the per cent

phases.win: the counter reads fifty, and the cards read 50/100 and 50%
phases.does: taps Split tenths, watches each column cut into ten, and types the per cent
phases.goal: each tenth is ten hundredths, so a number of tenths is ten times as many hundredths
phases.says: Each column is one tenth. Cut it into ten. How many hundredths now?
phases.check: Away from the screen: how many hundredths are in seven tenths?
phases.feels: each column breaking into ten small cells
phases.hands: Shade some whole columns of a paper grid for a number of tenths, then draw the lines that cut each column into ten cells, and count them.
phases.tries: First rung: count the cells of one split column. Second rung: count on through the other columns. Third rung: the same task with fewer tenths shaded, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the digit after the point is the only digit there
wrong.move: counts the tenths as hundredths, giving a per cent ten times too small
wrong.screen: Split tenths cuts each shaded column into ten cells, and the cells are counted one by one in amber beside the child's count

wrong.why: the white columns are just as easy to count
wrong.screen: each shaded column is numbered in turn, and the unshaded ones stay warm white and unnumbered

phases.screen: the card showing 0.5 over one grid with five columns shaded
phases.soWhat: each tenth is ten hundredths, so tenths become hundredths as ten times as many

phases.win: the counter reads one hundred and seventy, and the per cent card reads 170%, past 100%
phases.does: taps Read as hundredths, counts the whole grid and the columns of the second, and types the per cent
phases.goal: each whole is one hundred hundredths. So an amount above one whole is above 100%
phases.says: One whole grid is a hundred hundredths. Keep counting into the next.
phases.check: Away from the screen: is two and a half more or less than one hundred per cent? How do you know?
phases.feels: the count rolling past one hundred into the next grid
phases.hands: Lay out full paper grids for the wholes and one more grid for the part. Count one hundred for each full grid, then count on through the part.
phases.tries: First rung: count the full grids only, one hundred each. Second rung: count the part grid only. Third rung: the same task with one full grid, before more full grids return.

wrong.why: the zero looks like nothing, so it seems safe to drop
wrong.move: skips the zero that holds the tenths place
wrong.screen: the grey 0 is ringed in amber, and the part grid shows single cells with no full column, the columns counted as none

wrong.why: a full grid is one whole, and one is the number of wholes
wrong.move: counts a full grid as one, not one hundred
wrong.screen: the full grid's cells are counted in a quick amber sweep, and the counter climbs with them to one hundred

phases.screen: the card showing 1.7 over two grids, the first whole and the second empty
phases.soWhat: each whole is one hundred hundredths, so an amount above one whole is above one hundred per cent

phases.win: five full grids, and the line reads (5 x 100)% = 500%
phases.does: fills one whole grid for each whole, counts the lots of one hundred, and types the per cent
phases.goal: a whole number is that many lots of 100%
phases.says: Each whole is a hundred per cent. How many wholes are there?
phases.check: Away from the screen: how many full grids would show eight hundred per cent?
phases.feels: row after row of full grids, each one a hundred per cent
phases.hands: Lay one fully shaded paper grid for each whole of the whole number, and count one hundred per cent for each.
phases.tries: First rung: fill one whole grid and read its per cent. Second rung: fill one more and count on. Third rung: the same task with two wholes, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the number is the one on the card
wrong.move: types the whole number with the % sign straight after it
wrong.screen: each whole grid is labelled one hundred per cent in turn, and a second row shades what the child's answer names, only a few cells of one grid

wrong.why: one lot of one hundred was enough for one whole
wrong.move: counts one hundred once instead of once for each whole
wrong.screen: the grids fill one at a time, each ringed amber as it is counted, and the counter climbs one hundred for each

phases.screen: the card showing 5 and a row of empty whole grids
phases.soWhat: a whole number is that many lots of one hundred per cent

writeup.delight: On the third phase, the instant the first grid fills, it gives a small bounce and the count rolls on into the second grid without stopping, the per cent card ticking past one hundred.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing filled yet. On the first phase the decimal card sits over one empty grid, with the % sign tile in its tray. On the second the card shows tenths over a grid with whole columns shaded. On the third it shows a decimal above one over two grids. On the fourth it holds a whole number over a row of empty grids. One thing moves, once: the Read as hundredths button gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any decimal or whole number, read as hundredths, split into tenths and counted. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on hundredths, tenths, decimals above one and whole numbers as per cents.
voiceLines: A decimal, and hundred grids waiting to be filled.
Read it as hundredths. How many hundredths is it?
Each column is one tenth. Cut it into ten. How many hundredths now?
One whole grid is a hundred hundredths. Keep counting into the next.
Each whole is a hundred per cent. How many wholes are there?
A new decimal. How many hundredths is it?
Free play. Fill, split and count as many grids as you like.
Read it as hundredths again, one column at a time.
Every decimal became hundredths, and every answer kept its sign.

observations.why: a per cent counts hundredths, and so does the counter.
observations.soWhat: the number of hundredths is the per cent.
observations.observe: The Hundredths counter stopped at the number the per cent card showed.

observations.soWhat: tenths become hundredths as ten times as many.
observations.observe: Each split tenth became a column of ten counted cells.

observations.why: each whole is one hundred hundredths.
observations.soWhat: an amount above one whole is above one hundred per cent.
observations.observe: Once a grid was full, the count went on into the next grid, past one hundred.

observations.why: a number with no sign counts wholes.
observations.soWhat: the % sign carries the meaning, so it stays on the answer.
observations.observe: Until the sign tile was placed, the per cent card showed whole grids.

phases.screen: the card showing 0.62 over one empty grid, and the % sign tile beside the per cent card
phases.win: the counter stops at sixty-two, and the cards read 62/100 and 62%
phases.traceback: Each shaded column is counted 10 and each single cell 1, in amber, until the Hundredths and Per cent cards show the answer.
ladder: The 3 after the point is 3 full columns of 10 hundredths.
Each shaded column holds 10 hundredths, and each single cell is 1.
The 0 holds the tenths place, so no column is full.
The second digit after the point counts the single cells in the next column.
The count of shaded hundredths is the per cent, and the % sign is already there.

phases.screen: the card showing 0.5 over one grid with five columns shaded
phases.win: the counter reads fifty, and the cards read 50/100 and 50%
phases.traceback: Each shaded tenth is split into ten cells and counted ten at a time in amber, ending on the hundredths and the per cent.
ladder: Each shaded column is a tenth, which is 10 hundredths, not 1.
Count the shaded columns, and give each one 10 hundredths.
In 0.2 the 2 counts tenths, but in 0.02 it counts hundredths.
Picture each shaded column cut into ten cells, and count them all.
Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so the number of tenths times ten is the per cent.

phases.screen: the card showing 1.7 over two grids, the first whole and the second empty
phases.win: the counter reads one hundred and seventy, and the per cent card reads 170%, past 100%
phases.traceback: Each full grid is counted 100 in amber, then the part grid's columns and cells, ending on the hundredths and the per cent.
ladder: The 0 holds the tenths place, so the last grid has no full column.
A full grid is 100 hundredths, not 1.
Each shaded column of the part grid is a tenth, worth 10 hundredths.
Count 100 for each full grid, then count on into the part grid.
Put the hundredths of every grid together, and that number is the per cent.

phases.screen: the card showing 5 and a row of empty whole grids
phases.win: five full grids, and the line reads (5 x 100)% = 500%
phases.traceback: Each whole grid is ringed and counted 100% in turn, ending on (wholes × 100)% and the per cent.
ladder: Each whole grid is 100%, not 1%.
Count 100 for every whole, not for just one.
12 wholes are 12 full grids, and each grid is 100%.
Count 100% for each full grid, one grid at a time.
Multiply the number of wholes by 100, and the % sign is already there.

items.win: Yes, 0.56 is 56 hundredths, so it is 56%.
Yes, 0.9 is 9 tenths, which is 90 hundredths, so 90%.
Yes, 0.4 is 40 hundredths, so it is 40%.
Yes, 2.08 is 208 hundredths, so it is 208%.
Yes, 7 wholes are 7 lots of 100%, which is 700%.
Yes, 3 is 3 lots of 100%, so it is 300%.
Yes, 12 wholes are 12 lots of 100%, so 1,200%.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: Each shaded column is counted 10 and each single cell 1, in amber, until the Hundredths and Per cent cards show the answer.
Phase 2: Each shaded tenth is split into ten cells and counted ten at a time in amber, ending on the hundredths and the per cent.
Phase 3: Each full grid is counted 100 in amber, then the part grid's columns and cells, ending on the hundredths and the per cent.
Phase 4: Each whole grid is ringed and counted 100% in turn, ending on (wholes × 100)% and the per cent.

voice.opening: A decimal, and hundred grids waiting to be filled.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: read each decimal as hundredths, keep the % sign, then tap New.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Every decimal became hundredths, and every answer kept its sign.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

question.en: Now write 0.56 as a per cent.
Now write 0.4 as a per cent.

items.planAnswer: 40%, because 0.4 is 4 tenths, which is 40 hundredths
0.2 is 20 hundredths, so 20%. 0.02 is 2 hundredths, so 2%
360%, because 3 wholes are 300 hundredths and 6 tenths are 60 hundredths

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

getState: toolId, mediaId, mode, mountPhase, phase, phases, conceptId, objectiveIds, step, steps, item, items, stage (teach, demo, ask, win, idle, summary, free), question, questionText, choices, typed, keypadOpen, tries, answered, firstTry, score, maxScore, answerShown (only after the answer), complete, questionCount, muted (the sound effects), speaking (always false: the lesson is silent), voice ("silent"), mascot, summaryRow, played, classroom, held (a classroom's parked piece of a long line), instruction (the pinned line), hint (the hint under it, or null), guideStep / guideSteps / guideOn (a guide-steps phase only), decimal, grids, hundredths, split, split, sign_placed, answer, complete

terminalEvent.name: finished
terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first

sounds: Web Audio, no files, on in every mode (the sound button switches them): correct, wrong (soft), win at a phase end, cheer at the last, a tick when a piece snaps, and cut, settle and trade where the picture moves
